title: Our Lady of Lourdes: The Apparitions to St. Bernadette Soubirous in 1858
summary: From February 11 to July 16, 1858, the Blessed Virgin Mary appeared eighteen times to fourteen-year-old Bernadette Soubirous at the Grotto of Massabielle in Lourdes, France. Her message called for prayer, penance, conversion, and processions, identifying herself as the Immaculate Conception.

blocks.text: 1. Bernadette and the Historical Setting
Bernadette Soubirous was born on January 7, 1844, into a impoverished family in Lourdes, France. She had little formal education and was preparing for her First Communion when the apparitions began.
The encounters took place four years after Pope Pius IX defined the dogma of the Immaculate Conception in 1854, a profound connection that would become central to the Church's discernment.
2. The Eighteen Apparitions & Revelation of the Name
The apparitions began on February 11, 1858, at the Grotto of Massabielle. The Lady prayed the Rosary with Bernadette, establishing prayer and penance as the core of her message.

On February 25, Bernadette was instructed to scrape the earth near the back of the grotto, unearthing a miraculous spring that has since been linked to thousands of reported spiritual and physical healings.
On March 25, the feast of the Annunciation, Bernadette asked the Lady for her identity, receiving her answer in the local Gascon dialect.

blocks.title: Words of Our Lady to St. Bernadette (March 25, 1858)
blocks.text: “Que soy era Immaculada Concepciou” (“I am the Immaculate Conception”).
Bernadette later entered the Sisters of Charity of Nevers, living a quiet religious life until her death in 1879. She was canonized by Pope Pius XI on December 8, 1933.
The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.

Exegesis: The Gospel calls every soul to repentance and faith. Lourdes reflects this central biblical message: prayer, penance, and bodily healings are all meant to spur deep spiritual conversion in Christ.
3. The Message of Lourdes

The core message centers on prayer for sinners, penance, and sacramental life. The requests for a chapel and processions emphasize that the apparitions point back to the visible worship of the Church.
The title 'Immaculate Conception' reflects Mary's preservation from original sin from her first moment of existence, highlighting the fruits of Christ's redemptive grace.

blocks.title: The Spiritual Center
blocks.text: Lourdes is fundamentally a call to conversion. Physical healings are signs pointing toward Christ's greater spiritual gift: forgiveness of sins, inner peace, and sacramental grace.
4. Public vs. Private Revelation
Public Revelation was completed during the apostolic era. The apparitions at Lourdes are private revelation and do not add to the deposit of faith.

blocks.title: CCC 67: Private Revelation
blocks.text: Private revelations do not belong to the deposit of faith. Their role is not to improve or complete Christ's definitive Revelation, but to help Christians live by it more fully in a specific era.
5. Investigation and Official Approval
Following a rigorous four-year investigation into Bernadette's testimony and reported healings, Bishop Laurence of Tarbes formally approved devotion at the grotto on January 18, 1862.

Pope Pius X extended the feast of Our Lady of Lourdes to the universal Church in 1907. Today, alleged physical cures undergo exhaustive examination by the Lourdes Medical Bureau and ecclesial authorities.

blocks.title: Church Approval Status
blocks.text: Formally approved by the local bishop in 1862 and given universal liturgical recognition by Pope Pius X in 1907. St. Bernadette was canonized in 1933.
His mother said to the servants, 'Do whatever he tells you.'
Exegesis: At Massabielle as at Cana, Mary’s maternal role is intercessory and directional, continuously guiding the faithful into deeper obedience to her Son.
6. Pastoral Application

Devotion to Our Lady of Lourdes inspires special care for the sick and suffering. Practicing this devotion involves frequent participation in Mass, Reconciliation, Eucharistic Adoration, and works of mercy.

blocks.title: Central Lesson
blocks.text: Our Lady of Lourdes calls the Church to prayer, penance, and compassionate service to the sick, pointing all souls to Jesus Christ, who saves and heals.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer
blocks.text: O God of mercy, you made the Immaculate Virgin Mary a sign of hope for your pilgrim people. Through the intercession of Our Lady of Lourdes and St. Bernadette, deepen our faith in Jesus Christ, forgive our sins, and teach us to pray for sinners. Give strength to the sick and grace to all who suffer. Our Lady of Lourdes, pray for us. St. Bernadette, pray for us. Amen.
